reader.requirement: At --std 85 the OPTIONAL phrase takes effect only for an OPEN in input, I-O or extend mode: an absent optional file opens with 05 (created for I-O and extend, at end on the first READ for input), an absent non-optional file fails with 35, and OPEN OUTPUT of an optional file behaves exactly as of any file (created, 00); this holds for every organization whose SELECT may carry OPTIONAL at 85.
reader.edition-search: grep -n IsOptional over Runtime/IO/*.cs and Optional/OPTIONAL over Binding/FileControlBinder.cs and CobolIO.g4, then grep for DialectBehaviors.IsActive, Edition, DialectLevel on those members: the OPEN arms that read IsOptional (SequentialConnector#OpenCore, KeyedConnector#OpenCore) consult no edition and are the code every edition takes
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf19_01 covers a sequential file in every open mode and an absent non-optional input; relative and indexed OPTIONAL files and an optional file that is present are not exercised

reader.notes: The binder sets FileModel.Optional from the grammar's SELECT OPTIONAL token and the connector's IsOptional is read only in the INPUT, EXTEND and I-O arms of OpenCore; the OUTPUT arm ignores it, which is the rule's 'applies only'. The 1985 text gives 05 and creation for I-O and extend exactly as the code does.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-118/opt2.cob at --std 85 (opt2-001), aimed at what the reader did not try: OPEN INPUT of an absent optional file 05, READ 10, CLOSE 00 and the file is NOT created (a non-optional SELECT of the same name then answers 35); OPEN EXTEND of it 05 creates it and the record written is read back 00 E001 through the non-optional SELECT; OPEN OUTPUT of the now-present optional file 00 and truncates (READ 10), i.e. OPTIONAL has no effect in output mode; a RANDOM-access relative OPTIONAL file opened I-O absent 05, READ KEY 23, WRITE 00, read back by a second SELECT. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.2.3.4 GR2; OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.1.
